scope: A bounded map of calcific uraemic arteriolopathy: mineral-metabolism drivers, calcification-inhibitor deficiency (MGP/vitamin K, fetuin-A), vascular smooth-muscle osteogenic change, arteriolar calcification, thrombosis and skin ischaemic necrosis, plus curated therapies.

paragraphs.text: In haemodialysis patients, a lower carboxylated fraction of circulating matrix Gla protein was associated with higher odds of calciphylaxis, each 0.1-unit fall in relative cMGP corresponding to more than a two-fold higher risk; the association persisted in patients not taking warfarin. Medial calcification and other historically 'characteristic' findings also occurred in viable skin of ESRD patients without calciphylaxis; only the combination of medial calcification with thrombosis was rare in unaffected patients (six-fold more prevalent in high-suspicion biopsies). Mice lacking matrix Gla protein develop spontaneous arterial and cartilage calcification and die of blood-vessel rupture within two months, establishing MGP as an active inhibitor of soft-tissue and arterial calcification produced by vascular smooth muscle cells.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Very small case-control (n=40) from a single programme; wide uncertainty around the risk estimate MGP measured at or after diagnosis, so reverse causation and illness effects cannot be excluded In the phase 3 CALCIPHYX RCT (n=71), wound score (BWAT-CUA) and pain VAS improved similarly with hexasodium fytate and placebo at week 12 (BWAT-CUA LS mean difference 0.3, p=0.88; pain VAS difference 11.5, p=0.15); neither primary endpoint was met. Drug targeting and approval do not establish every proposed mechanism or benefit in every phenotype.
